source: NCERT Class VII, Our Environment, Geography Ch. 1.

sections.heading: 1. What is Environment
points: **Environment** = our surroundings — everything (living and non-living) around us that affects life.
It includes **natural, human and human-made** components interacting together.
The place where plants, animals and humans live and interact = **habitat/ecosystem**.

sections.heading: 2. Natural Environment — Four Domains
points: **Lithosphere** — the solid **land/crust** (mountains, plateaus, plains); source of minerals and soil.
**Hydrosphere** — all **water** (oceans, rivers, lakes, groundwater).
**Atmosphere** — the **air** (blanket of gases) around the Earth.
**Biosphere** — the narrow zone where land, water and air **meet and support life** (plants, animals, humans).

sections.heading: 3. Human and Human-made Environment
points: **Human environment** — people and their activities, needs and society.
**Human-made environment** — things built by humans: buildings, roads, dams, cities, parks, industries.
Humans **interact with and modify** the natural environment (farming, mining, building) — which must be done **sustainably**.

sections.heading: 4. Ecosystem
points: **Ecosystem** = a community of **living organisms** interacting with the **non-living (physical) environment**.
Examples: a forest, a pond, a desert.
All parts are **interdependent**; disturbing one part affects the whole.

sections.heading: 5. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Environment = natural + human + human-made surroundings.
Four natural domains: lithosphere (land), hydrosphere (water), atmosphere (air), biosphere (life zone).
Biosphere = where land, water & air meet to support life.
Ecosystem = living organisms + non-living environment interacting.
Human-made environment = buildings, roads, dams, cities.

sections.heading: 6. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Lithosphere = land**, **hydrosphere = water**, **atmosphere = air**, **biosphere = life zone** — don't swap.
The **biosphere** is where all three other domains **overlap** to make life possible.
An **ecosystem** includes BOTH living and non-living components interacting.
